issues.title: Non-strict inequality operator used
issues.description: The rule requires using strict equality operators (=== or !==) for all comparisons, but the code uses != instead of !== to check if count is null
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
const count = result.data[0].get('csd_email_count');
return count != null ? count : 0;
issues.rule_name: Code Must Use Strict Equality Operators

issues.title: Date filter includes today's emails instead of excluding them
issues.description: The filter in #getHighestCount() uses `created_at:<=` which includes today's date, but the docstring explicitly states it should exclude today. This causes the method to potentially return today's partial email count instead of the previous day's complete count. When emails are sent early in the day, this will result in a lower base count for warmup limit calculations, causing the domain warming progression to restart or regress unexpectedly. This breaks the intended day-over-day scaling behavior where each day's limit should be based on the previous day's complete sending volume.

issues.title: High-volume threshold boundary applies wrong scaling factor at 400k
issues.description: The condition uses `>=` instead of `>` when checking if lastCount qualifies for high-volume capping at exactly 400,000 emails. According to the documented scaling table, 400k should use the 2× multiplier from the thresholds array, but with this bug it immediately applies the high-volume cap of 1.2× or +75k absolute increase. For a site hitting exactly 400k messages, this means getting a limit of 480k (1.2×) or 475k (+75k) instead of the expected 800k (2×). This creates a significant bottleneck at a critical growth milestone and breaks the documented warmup progression.

issues.title: Threshold boundary values skip their designated scaling tier
issues.description: The loop uses `<` instead of `<=` when comparing lastCount to threshold limits. This causes exact boundary values (1000, 5000, 100000, 400000) to incorrectly skip their tier and fall through to the next scaling factor or the fallback logic. For example, a site with exactly 1000 previous emails will bypass the 1.25× tier and incorrectly use 1.5× scaling (getting 1500 instead of 1250). Similarly, 5000 will use 1.75× instead of 1.5×, and 100000 will use 2× instead of 1.75×. This creates unexpected jumps in scaling at precisely the documented threshold boundaries.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25526 - Updated the scaling factors for domain warmup

structured_output.summary:
This PR swaps the old warmup curve (2× up to 100k, 1.5× up to 400k, then 1.25×) for a gentler one: 1.25× up to 1k, 1.5× up to 5k, 1.75× up to 100k, and 2× up to 400k. Above 400k, growth is capped at min(1.2×, +75k). It also changes `#getHighestCount` to use `findPage({limit: 1})` instead of `findOne`, and pins the integration-test clock to a fixed base date.

The new table is sensible, but the code doesn't do what the PR's own tests and docs say. The threshold check changed from `<=` to `<`, and the high-volume branch fires at `>= 400_000`. That pushes every boundary value into the next tier: 1000 → 1500 (expected 1250), 5000 → 8750 (expected 7500), 100000 → 200000 (expected 175000), 400000 → 475000 (expected 800000). Four progression cases and the "calculated limit" test will fail. Separately, the date filter quietly changed from `created_at:<today` to `created_at:<=today`. That contradicts the "excluding today" docstring and fails the unit test that checks for the `<` filter.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Boundary comparisons in `#getTargetLimit` don't match the documented table or the PR's own unit tests, so five unit tests fail. The history filter also changed from `<` to `<=`, which breaks the "before today" contract and its test.

architecture.overview:
When a newsletter is sent, `EmailService` asks `DomainWarmingService.getWarmupLimit(emailCount)` how many recipients should go through the custom sending domain (CSD). The service looks up the highest `csd_email_count` from earlier emails, runs it through a tiered scaling table to get today's target, and returns the smaller of that target and the real recipient count. The result is saved on the Email row as `csd_email_count`, and `BatchSendingService` uses it later to split batches between domains.

This PR changes the lookup from `Email.findOne` to `Email.findPage({limit: 1})` so the `order` clause actually applies. It also replaces the scaling table with five tiers plus a `highVolume` branch that caps growth at min(1.2×, +75k) once the previous count reaches 400k.
steps: Start in `EmailService.js` (~line 129): when the `domainWarmup` lab flag is on, it calls `getWarmupLimit(emailCount)` and saves the result as `csd_email_count` on the new Email row.
`DomainWarmingService.#getHighestCount` now calls `Email.findPage` with a date filter, `csd_email_count DESC` ordering, and `limit: 1`, then reads `csd_email_count` from the first row.
`#getTargetLimit` returns 200 for counts ≤100. Counts ≥400k go to the `highVolume` cap. Everything else walks the sorted `thresholds` list and applies the first matching tier's multiplier.
`getWarmupLimit` clamps the target to the actual recipient count.
Tests: the unit tests use `createModelClass({findAll: [...]})`, whose `findPage` mock slices `findAll`. The integration tests send real emails on fake-timer days and check exact CSD counts.

findings.title: Strict `<` comparison and `>= 400k` branch push boundary values into the wrong tier
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/DomainWarmingService.ts` `#getTargetLimit` (lines 124-135), boundary values fall into the wrong tier: lastCount=1000 returns 1500 (expected 1250), 5000→8750 (expected 7500), 100000→200000 (expected 175000), 400000→475000 (expected 800000). Change the thresholds loop comparison from `lastCount < threshold.limit` to `lastCount <= threshold.limit`, and change the high-volume check from `>=` to `>` so 400k still uses 2×. Then run `test/unit/server/services/email-service/domain-warming-service.test.ts` and confirm every case in the progression table (lines ~196-209) passes.

findings.title: History filter changed to `<=` today, contradicting "excluding today" and the unit test
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/DomainWarmingService.ts` line 102, the `#getHighestCount` filter changed from `created_at:<${today}` to `created_at:<=${today}`. That contradicts the method's "excluding today" docstring and fails the unit test at `test/unit/server/services/email-service/domain-warming-service.test.ts:181`, which checks for `created_at:<${today}`. Restore the strict `<` operator so only emails from before today count toward the highest CSD count.

findings.title: Duplicated 400k boundary and an unreachable fallback can drift apart
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/DomainWarmingService.ts`, the 400_000 boundary appears in both `WARMUP_SCALING_TABLE.thresholds` (last entry) and `highVolume.threshold`, and the fallback at lines 136-138 returns an uncapped 1.2× that skips the +75k cap. Pull the high-volume cap into a small helper and call it from both the `highVolume` branch and the fallback, so the cap always applies. Optionally sort `thresholds` once at definition instead of calling `.sort()` on every call.

findings.title: Switching to findPage makes the ORDER BY actually apply
findings.body:
Moving from `findOne` to `findPage({order, limit: 1})` is a good change. Ghost's `findOne` is built for lookups by attributes, not for sorted queries. `findPage` reliably applies `csd_email_count DESC` and limits the result to one row. The explicit `count != null ? count : 0` is also clearer than `count || 0`.

findings.title: Integration tests now assert exact values
findings.body:
The multi-day integration test used to accept "same, doubled, or total". It now checks exact values (200 → 250 → 313), which actually exercises the `Math.ceil` rounding. Pinning `setDay` to a fixed `baseDate` with `shouldAdvanceTime` also gets rid of day-rollover flakiness.
